ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Resource-normalized throughput of any H1-H8 system on p workers is bounded by T_p >= max(W/p, S, ceil(n/b) * c_batch): W = total verification/generation work, S = span of the input dependency DAG, and ceil(n/b) * c_batch = the BATCHED AMORTIZED serialization floor for appending n accountable transitions through the single logical serialization point (H4/H6) in batches of b — batched Merkle appends amortize to O(1) hashing per item with O(log n) proof material per append, so the floor is per-BATCH serialization, not per-transition ('irreducibly serial per transition' is retracted). Verification work W has an operative floor under the declared toolchain: a zero-producer-trust verifier in recompute mode must read and hash every committed byte at least once, so throughput is capped by min(I/O bandwidth, hash bandwidth) per admitted byte; on unchanged inputs, content-addressed memoization reduces work to the delta plus one digest comparison per cached unit. Sublinear verification via succinct TRANSPARENT proof systems (no trusted setup; hash-family assumptions) is not cryptographically excluded — its absence here is a declared-toolchain/arithmetization cost fact, which is exactly what the RESOURCE_BOUNDED kind records. The ceiling is attained by deterministic parallel-map with ordered serial fold; all bounds derived from committed corpus configuration, never constants.
derivation: (1) Serialization floor, corrected: H4 plus H6 force a total order on admissions — one logical serialization point (physical single writer, or machine-checked nonforking replicated order); commit throughput is bounded by that point's sequential rate, and the optimum is batched commitment: group b transitions per batch, one serialized append per batch, per-item cost one hash amortized, O(log n) proof material — hence the floor ceil(n/b) * c_batch, which the attainment schedule itself uses. (2) Work/span law (Brent): any p-worker schedule has makespan >= max(W/p, S) — implementation-independent. (3) Verification floor, restated honestly: under zero producer trust in RECOMPUTE mode, trusting k bytes requires reading k bytes (Omega(k) I/O and hashing). The v1 exclusion of succinct proofs by 'trusted setup' was false — STARK-class systems are transparent; the honest exclusion ground is toolchain/arithmetization cost only, so the linear floor is OPERATIVE (toolchain-relative), not absolute — consistent with the AX-06/AX-13 v2 split. (4) Determinism costs nothing asymptotically: parallel-map with deterministic ordered reduction achieves the same T_p bound with byte-identical output — any design paying throughput for determinism is below ceiling.
relativity_note: The linear verification floor and the batch constant c_batch are relative to the declared toolchain and storage/hash bandwidth; the work/span law and the existence of a serialization floor are model-independent.
lean_obligation: Theorem (schedule optimality with batched accountable commit): for a dependency DAG with work W and span S, and a total-ordered commit relation with per-batch cost c_batch and batch size b, every conforming p-worker schedule satisfies T_p >= max (W/p) (max S (ceil(n/b) * c_batch)), and the ordered-parallel-map/serial-fold schedule achieves T_p <= W/p + S + ceil(n/b) * c_batch with output extensionally equal to the sequential schedule. Amortization lemma: total hashing over n batched appends is O(n) with O(log n) proof material per append. Verification floor lemma (recompute mode): a sound zero-producer-trust recomputing verifier over committed bytes b reads at least |b| positions (indistinguishability of strings differing at an unread index). Incremental floor: unchanged cached unit re-verifies in exactly one digest comparison.

attainment_witness_appendix.candidate_mechanism: B0 witness seats: lparallel one-file-per-article work tier; the single-writer commit seat feeding RFC-6962 Merkle appends; content-addressed memoization (artifact-cache.lisp); the 3000-event chain as a scale demonstration. Steps: (a) replace error-swallowing with fail-closed per-tier all-or-nothing completion; (b) deterministic ordered reduction (merge by article index before commit); (c) derive the article bound from corpus configuration instead of the literal type bound; (d) persist throughput into the AX-17 hash-chained ledger so scale claims are replayable artifacts; (e) batch the Merkle appends to realize the amortized floor.
attainment_witness_appendix.b0_gap_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: frbr-pipeline-stage.lisp hardcodes (integer 1 120) type declarations (an artificial scale cliff no ceiling argument permits); parallel-executor swallows errors and has nondeterministic intra-tier order (throughput bought by breaking H3/H5 — below ceiling by definition); no persisted throughput ledger, so present scale claims are not offline-verifiable.
